factual_errors.claim: Framing the problem as the converter simply lacking 'protocol interpretation'/framing, addressable by checking baud/parity/stop-bits/wiring/termination
factual_errors.why_wrong: A transparent RS-485-to-Ethernet converter cannot ever run DH-485 regardless of configuration: DH-485 requires token-passing network arbitration and a TX-EN (transmit-enable) open-collector control line for half-duplex turnaround that a transparent converter has no way to provide. This is an architectural incompatibility, not a settings mismatch, so the suggested config checks will not resolve it.

factual_errors.claim: No mention that the DH-485 RJ45/port uses 0-5V RS-485 signal levels, distinct from Ethernet voltage levels
factual_errors.why_wrong: Connecting standard Ethernet-side equipment to a DH-485 port that expects 0-5V RS-485 levels carries a real equipment-damage risk (network card / PLC processor). Omitting this warning is a safety-adjacent gap for a customer performing this swap without knowing the risk.

factual_errors.claim: The definitive fix (reinstall the original protocol-aware interface, or replace with an equivalent like a 1747-AIC/1761-NET-AIC) is only offered as a conditional troubleshooting step, not stated as the answer
factual_errors.why_wrong: Given the converter can never work on DH-485, the technician needs to be told directly that a protocol-aware interface is required, not led through a multi-step diagnostic first.
